newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Laotian trafficker awaits word on Vietnam pardon.
newsitem.headline: Laotian trafficker awaits word on Vietnam pardon.

text.p: A convicted Laotian drugs trafficker whose confessions played a key part in Vietnam's biggest narcotics trial earlier this year, still awaited word on Tuesday on whether he would be spared the firing squad.
State media reported that President Le Duc Anh had issued instructions in late July commuting the death sentence against the trafficker, Sieng Pheng, to life.
But officials at the presidential office expressed surprise at the news. They said no decision had been made and added they were inquiring to see where the reports had come from.
Sieng Pheng was sentenced to death after being found guilty of trying to smuggle 15 kg (33 pounds) of heroin into Vietnam in 1995 hidden in a secret compartment of a car.
But he broke down shortly before he was due to be executed and offered to exchange information in return for his life being spared.
The evidence he supplied was used in a major court case in May in which eight people, including police officials and border guards, were sentenced to death.

The notoriety of the lead defendant, former policeman Vu Xuan Truong, turned him into a virtual celebrity, prompting humour in July when an official of the same name in northern Vietnam's Thai Binh province succeeded in being elected to parliament.

A total of around 60 people were arrested in connection with the case and a second trial involving some of those had been scheduled to take place last month. It was postponed indefinitely at the last moment for unknown reasons.
